title: Comparison-flow decomposition
description: The bands the homepage room disperses into. DESIGN.md section 11 state 1: one collimated beam enters a dispersing element and leaves as bands whose widths are the real component magnitudes. Generated by scripts/build_data.py from one evidence record, bound by DECISIONS.md D-37 to campaign.result.TOPO-HODGE. RE-POINTED AT BUILD TIME: the first subject was per-category benchmark accuracy, five accuracies on five slices whose sum has no referent, and it was withdrawn because the figure asserts composition and that set does not compose. What is dispersed now is one grader's comparison energy, split into three orthogonal subspaces that sum to exactly 1. THE BAND COUNT IS THE DATA'S: tokens.css:228 defines six component colours because a decomposition shows at most six at once, and this one has three, so --comp-4 through --comp-6 stay unused. GROUND-TRUTH.md C-7. Padding to six is the same defect as a hand-set count. NO LABELS ARE CARRIED HERE: each band emits `part`, and copy.yaml binds the display string, because naming what the figure asserts is a copy decision.

excludesNote.description: Which reported number is deliberately NOT a band, and why. Required, because the exclusion is invisible in the data and a later reader adding the fourth band back would double-count.

quantityStoreLabel.description: The record's own label for itself, for a provenance panel. STORE ONLY: it contains a campaign card id, which data/banned-terms.json bans from rendered text, so it is not the figure's caption and a renderer that prints it fails gate 7. RENAMED FROM `quantity` at build time, because the shorter name read like something a caption could use.

fanDegrees.description: How wide the fan opens. The only rendering constant in this file, and it decides nothing about where the bands sit inside it, which is entirely the magnitudes'.

angleRule.description: The derivation, stated in the data rather than hidden in a renderer, so a reader of this file can check that the angles follow from the magnitudes. It must also state what the derivation does at a vanishing share, because this decomposition has one.

bands.description: At most six, because there are six component tokens. Never padded to six and never truncated. Ordered as the decomposition derives them, so position carries identity independently of hue.

part.description: The key the decomposition uses for this part. A key and not a label: copy.yaml binds the display string. A band carrying prose here is a component inventing user-facing text.

componentToken.description: DESIGN.md section 5.4. Assigned by position in the derivation's order.

magnitude.description: As measured. Never floored, clamped or rounded away: this decomposition has a part at 2.4e-31 and that value is the finding.

exitAngle.description: Degrees from the fan axis. Derived from share, never chosen.

angularWidth.description: MINIMUM ZERO, NOT EXCLUSIVE MINIMUM. Widened at build time: a band whose measured share is 2.4e-31 has a width of 5.8e-30 degrees, and a part measured at exactly zero would have a width of exactly zero. Both are findings and neither may be excluded by a schema.

belowFloat64Epsilon.description: True where the share is smaller than float64 machine epsilon (2.220446049250313e-16) against a total of 1, meaning the band is below the precision of the arithmetic that produced it. It is a measured absence rather than a measured small number, and that is what licenses rendering it as a labelled absence rather than as a sliver. Derived, not a display threshold and not a guess about pixels.

derivedTotals.description: Numbers the source record reports that are sums of the bands rather than bands. Held here so they are available and cannot be rendered as parts. For the Hodge split that is intransitiveMass, which is curl + harmonic (hodge.py:441-442, 'reported only beside its two parts, never instead of them').

closure.description: Why there is no conservation residual to render. Unlike the credit disintegration, which reports its closure as a number, hodge.py:558-566 ASSERTS orthogonality, reconstruction and unit mass before returning, and escalates a sparse solve to a dense one rather than returning a decomposition it cannot certify. Closure is a precondition of the number existing.

perDataset.description: TWO DECOMPOSITIONS, NOT SIX PARTS. The source record splits its result by dataset, and each dataset carries its own complete three-way split. Concatenating them to reach six bands would invent a decomposition nobody measured. Held outside `bands` so a renderer cannot reach them as ones. EVERYTHING HERE COMES FROM A DIFFERENT RECORD FROM THE BANDS: the per-dataset splits are only on the payload record, which the site's evidence store does not carry, so DECISIONS.md D-35 applies and a document and line take the place of an id. `home.decomposition.scope`'s tournament count binds to `tournamentsEach` and renders that citation, not a chip.

evidenceId.description: Null, and it is typed as null rather than nullable: the payload record is filtered out of the site's store by construction, so an id here would never resolve and no future run can make one appear.

observable.description: Store only. It contains a campaign card id and is banned from rendered text.

tournamentsEach.description: copy.yaml:home.figure.decomposition.scope reads '{{tournament_count}} tournaments each', which is one number over several datasets. Derived, and null when the datasets disagree, so the scope line loses its number rather than reporting one dataset's count as all of them.

evidenceId.description: Populated. This record has one, unlike the run series, whose numbers resolve to a frozen document instead.

trust.description: The rung WORD, one of the four in data/refusals.json's ladder. It was the rung integer stringified, which renders as "trust 2" and carries no --trust-* colour.

trustRung.description: The same rung as the integer the store wrote, beside the word rather than instead of it.
